whyTitle:
From what we know,
to something better
originFirst: I remember learning Spring Boot: complex dependency management, a heavy runtime, and security settings that felt difficult. Before building a product, I had to wrestle with the framework.
originSecond:
Do we have to leave years of experience behind?
Keep the familiar structure and simplify its abstractions and execution. That question started Spine.
mapLabel: Connecting familiar development patterns to new technology
learned: What you knowControllers, services, dependency injection
newPossibilities: What comes nextMore possibilities with fewer resources
originClosing: Keep what you learned. Expand what you can do.
frameworkFirst:
Controllers, services, and constructor injection.
Bring familiar patterns to Go.
frameworkSecond: Spine is a backend framework that makes execution order and responsibility visible in code. Read how a request is interpreted and executed.
bindingDescription: Declare each input source with input.Path[T], input.Query[T], input.Header[T], or input.Body[T]. Dereference the path wrapper to read its value.
interceptorDescription: Separate shared concerns with hooks receiving spine.Ctx. After PreHandle, return-value processing and PostHandle lead to BeforeResponse and AfterCompletion.
controllerDescription: The controller receives input.Path[int] and delegates work to a service. Express success with httpx.Response[T] and failure with error.
responseDescription: Set the body and status through Body and Options in httpx.Response[T]. An HTTP callback returns one response and an optional error.
frameworkStatement:
Unfamiliar tools should never
keep better technology out of reach.
performanceDescription: Everyone should have access to safe, fast technology. A lighter runtime matters when resources are limited. High performance should be within reach beyond specialized environments.
cloudTitle:

cloudFirst:

cloudSecond: Everyone deserves a chance to share what they make. Spine Cloud connects the first step of building to deployment.

licenseIntro: Sources and licenses for the 3D models, map, and fonts used on this site.
licenseChanges: Selected 24 vertebrae, one sacrum, and 23 discs from BodyParts3D 4.0. We transformed axes and scale, set per-part pivots, and applied ivory bone and mint disc materials. We provide a GLB model and PNG fallback; the view crops to the middle of the spine. No endorsement by the original provider is implied. In the web 3D view, discs use vermilion to match the site palette.
licenseHistory: Original OBJ headers retain an older CC BY-SA 2.1 Japan notice. NOTICE.txt preserves that history alongside the provider's current CC BY 4.0 notice.
licenseMapDescription: The globe's coastlines use Natural Earth's 1:110m land data. Natural Earth data is public domain; this site renders it as outlines on a 3D sphere.
licenseFontsDescription: Noto Sans KR and Schibsted Grotesk are used under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. Their original licenses are included.
betaRegion: The open beta is currently available in South Korea.

sunriseLabel: Five adventurers in a U-shaped formation, open at the front, looking up at the sun
licensePeopleDescription: Clothed characters from Kay Lousberg’s KayKit Adventurers are used under CC0. We keep the clothing and textures of Knight, Mage, Rogue, and Rogue_Hooded and hide weapon props. Unused animation data is removed to reduce file size. Five figures are scaled and posed to look up toward the sun. The sun and terrain are composed in Three.js.
